# Mesh exchange matrix — third-party verification (6 formats × 3 geometries)

Anchor: `GAP-CAD-B2-MESH-FORMAT-MATRIX` — *meshio 全格式矩阵进出（STL/OBJ/VTK/SU2/CGNS/Gmsh）*,
acceptance: 往返保真：体积/拓扑/取向不变（6 格式 × 3 几何 = 18 组合全绿表）.

Verifier seat (`tp-ver-8`), branch `agent/m22715`.

## 1. What the existing matrix proves — and what it does not

`tests/test_meshio_format_matrix.py` (141 passed, 4 skipped) writes every mesh with
**meshio** and reads it back with **meshio**. A writer and a reader that share a
private convention — a swapped byte order, an offset count, an element-tag column,
a cell-type code — agree with each other and the table still looks green while a
different tool reads the same bytes differently or not at all. Volume/topology/
orientation "preserved" therefore only proved *self*-consistency.

Two further weaknesses in that evidence:

* orientation was checked as `sign(volume)` only. Two opposite facet flips cancel;
  even a *single* flip of a facet whose plane passes through the origin changes the
  divergence-theorem sum by exactly zero. Both cases are reproduced as tests here
  (`test_harness_detects_a_flipped_facet` shows `ΔV = 0.0` for a flipped bottom
  facet of the unit cube).
* the STL volume tolerance was 1e-3, a leftover from an assumption that STL stores
  float32 positions. The files meshio writes are **ASCII** STL, so the real error is
  0 and 1e-3 could hide a genuine loss.

## 2. Method

New module `tensorcad/mesh_interop_independent.py` parses the on-disk bytes from the
format specifications alone — **no meshio, no `tensorcad.mesh_cgns`** (enforced by
`test_verifier_module_is_independent_of_meshio`, which imports the module in a
subprocess and asserts `meshio` never enters `sys.modules`):

| format | dialect parsed | independent parser |
|---|---|---|
| STL | ASCII `solid`/`facet normal`/`outer loop` | text records, per-facet normals kept |
| OBJ | `v` / `f`, 1-based indices | text records |
| VTK | legacy 5.1, `BINARY`, big-endian arrays, `OFFSETS`/`CONNECTIVITY` | byte-level, dtype from the header |
| Gmsh | MSH 4.1, binary, entity blocks, `elementTag + nodeTags` per element | byte-level |
| SU2 | ASCII `NDIME`/`NPOIN`/`NELEM`, VTK type codes, no element id | text records |
| CGNS | HDF5/SIDS: `Base/Zone/GridCoordinates/CoordinateX/ data`, `GridElements` | `h5py` node traversal |

Invariants asserted from those bytes:

1. **volume** — divergence-theorem surface volume / sum of tet determinants,
   compared with the reference mesh *and* with the analytic volume of the fixture;
2. **topology** — cell count equal to the reference; additionally, per-format
   self-consistency: gmsh element tags must run `1..N`, VTK `CELL_TYPES` must be
   `5` (triangle) / `10` (tetra), CGNS `CellDimension` must agree with the cell width;
3. **orientation** — `oriented_signature()`: every cell is keyed by its sorted vertex
   coordinates and carries the sign of its own winding (facet normal or tet
   determinant sign). Signatures are compared as multisets, so *per-cell* winding is
   verified while staying independent of vertex numbering (STL legitimately
   renumbers and duplicates vertices);
4. **format identity** — magic/records that a conforming reader relies on
   (HDF5 magic + `CGNSLibraryVersion`, `# vtk DataFile Version`, `$MeshFormat 4.1`,
   `NDIME=`, `solid`/`endsolid`, `v`/`f`);
5. **STL redundancy** — the stored facet normal must agree with the winding
   (`min cos = 1.0 - O(1e-16)`).

Fixtures (3, as the acceptance states): unit cube (V = 1 exact), capsule — closed
body of revolution, V = πr²L + 4/3πr³ = 3.665191429, Wigley hull from
`tensorcad.wigley` (V = 4LBT/9 = 2.777778, 1001 vertices / 1998 facets).

Reading of the table:

* **all 18 combinations pass**; volume relative error is **0.0** for every one of
  them (not merely "small"): each format stores float64/ASCII at full precision, so
  the recovered volume is bit-identical to the reference mesh's;
* the six formats agree with each other for the same geometry (`test_volume_matches_
  across_all_formats`), which is the property that makes this an *equivalence*
  rather than six unrelated round-trips;
* SU2/CGNS rows carry 1996 tets for the Wigley hull vs 1998 surface facets — the
  tetrahedraliser drops the two edge-on stem/post facets that span zero volume
  (documented in `meshio_exchange.TetrahedralMesh.edge_on_facets`); volume is
  unaffected to 3e-15;
* STL is the one documented topology limitation: it is a triangle soup, so it
  returns 3 × facets vertices (capsule: 4608 = 3 × 1536). Facet-level topology and
  winding are still verified. The claim in the ledger is therefore "volume/topology/
  orientation preserved" — for STL, topology is preserved at facet level only, and
  the test states this explicitly instead of skipping the row.

## 5. Notes, limitations, pitfalls

* **Dialect findings while writing the parsers** (each cost one debugging round and is
  now encoded with a comment): VTK 5.1 as written by meshio/ParaView declares the
  number of *offsets* (cells + 1), not the number of cells, in the `CELLS` header;
  legacy VTK binary arrays are **big-endian** while STL/OBJ/SU2 are text; MSH 4.1
  element records carry an `elementTag` before the node tags (I first mis-parsed
  this as a non-conforming file — it is conforming, MSH 4.0 differs here); CGNS/SIDS
  stores values in a child node literally named `" data"` with a leading blank, so
  `node["data"]` fails on conforming files.
* **Scope**: only the dialects `write_meshio` actually emits are parsed (ASCII STL,
  legacy VTK 5.1 binary, MSH 4.1 binary, ASCII SU2, HDF5 CGNS). Binary STL, ASCII
  MSH 4.1, MSH 2.2, VTK XML (`.vtu`) are **not** verified here and the readers raise
  `IndependentReadError` rather than guessing.
* **No external CAD/solver tool was executed**: `gmsh`, Salome, ParaView are not
  installed in this worktree, so "another tool can read it" is evidenced by
  spec-conformance of the bytes plus independent parsing, not by running that tool.
  That is the honest ceiling of this verification.
* Discretisation error is *not* an exchange error: capsule 0.70 %, Wigley 0.24 %
  against the analytic volumes, identical across all formats.

## 6. Error verdict

| quantity | reference | worst observed | criterion | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| volume, all 18 combinations | reference mesh volume | 0.0 (exact) | < 1e-12 | PASS |
| volume vs analytic, cube | 1.0 | 0.0 | < 1e-12 | PASS |
| volume vs analytic, capsule | 3.665191429 | 7.02e-3 (discretisation) | < 1 % | PASS |
| volume vs analytic, Wigley hull | 2.777778 | 2.36e-3 (discretisation) | < 1 % | PASS |
| cell count | reference count | 0 cells lost | exact | PASS |
| per-cell winding | reference signature | identical multiset | exact | PASS |
| STL stored normal vs winding | geometric normal | cos = 1.0 | ≥ 1 - 1e-9 | PASS |

**Is the key quantity within 3 %?** Yes — with margin: exchange error is exactly 0,
and the largest deviation from an analytic reference (0.70 %, capsule) is
discretisation of the faceted fixture, not a format loss, and is identical in all
six formats.

## 7. Reproduction

```
python -m pytest tests/test_mesh_format_matrix_thirdparty.py -q      # 54 passed
python -m pytest tests/test_meshio_format_matrix.py -q               # 141 passed, 4 skipped
python docs/mesh_format_matrix_thirdparty/run_campaign.py            # regenerates table + figure
```
